output.question: In 9.1.6, why do some eBGP routes stay in the table but show unresolved next hop after the connected route flaps?
output.reference_answer: On Aurora AR-900 9.1.6, this is caused by a BGP next-hop recursion cache issue in the 9.1 family. If the resolving connected or static underlay route is withdrawn and relearned within the 30-second hold interval, the cache can keep a stale negative resolution entry, so the session stays Established but the affected eBGP IPv4 prefixes remain in the table with an unresolved next hop until BGP is cleared or a new update triggers recursion. The issue affects 9.1.4 and 9.1.6 and is fixed in 9.2.0.
